articleTitle: The Design of a Directional Coupler Made on Microstrip Structures
abstract: The article considers models of directional couplers obtained on segments and microstrip structures. For a compact coupler, optimization of its parameters was used to adjust the characteristics to those similar to the standard design. The use of structures instead of quarter-wave segments is justified by the fact that they have similar characteristics at smaller sizes. This fact allows them to be used for miniaturization of connectors. Thus, we managed to obtain a compact design of the coupler with a 72.5% smaller area than its standard implementation. At the same time, the topology of the device has technologically feasible dimensions.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective MIMO precoding in Time Domain
abstract: The paper discusses methods of MIMO wireless channel precoder design (beamforming vector). Both the receiver and the transmitter have multiple antennas. Increasing antenna number of MIMO system is following to complicate procedure of precoders design. Many recent studies are aimed to find efficient precoding algorithm in term of low computational complexity for wide band transmission. Beamforming vector is calculated in frequency domain per each independent sub-band in order to utilize frequency division duplexing for OFDM based MIMO communication system. The representation of channel measurements in time domain is more compact than in frequency domain. This property is used in the proposed algorithm. The article presents algorithm (without significant loss of spatial efficiency) beamforming vectors design based on the it's calculation by selected channel impulse response taps. The proposed algorithm has a large potential in the computational complexity reduction of ordinary approach and achieves gain up to 35%.

articleTitle: A Study of the Impact of the Contention Window on the Performance of IEEE 802.11bd Networks with Channel Bonding
abstract: Nowadays, Vehicle-To-Everything (V2X) networks are actively developing. Most of the already deployed V2X networks are based on the IEEE 802.11p standard. However, these networks can provide only basic V2X applications and will unlikely fulfill stringent requirements of modern V2X applications. Thus, the IEEE has launched a new IEEE 802.11bd standard. A significant novelty of this standard is channel bonding. IEEE 802.11bd describes two channel bonding techniques, which differ from the legacy one used in modern WiFi networks. Our study performs a comparative analysis of the various channel bonding techniques and a single-channel access method from IEEE 802.11p via simulation. We compare them under different contention window sizes and demonstrate that the legacy technique provides the best quality of service in terms of frame transmission delays and packet loss ratio. Moreover, we have found a quasi-optimal contention window size for the legacy technique.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Planar Antenna with Optimized Slots and DGS for UWB Applications
abstract: Microstrip antennas are utilized in applications where size, weight, cost, and performance are limited. Microstrip antennas (MSA) are utilized in a variety of government and commercial applications, the most common of which being wireless communication. A miniature rectangular shape planar antenna with defective ground structure (DGS) is conceived for ultrawideband applications under this article. The proposed antenna is printed on FR4 substrate material and has an overall dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17\ \text{mm}\times 10\ \text{mm}\times 1.6\ \text{mm}$</tex>. It works over the UWB frequency range and has a bandwidth of 5.75 GHz to 12.86 GHz. This presented antenna has a peak gain of 5.4 dB and radiation efficiency of 98% efficiency. The compact antenna is a basic overlay design comprising rectangular patches and optimized slots with a partial ground plane that exhibits good gain and improved directivity.

articleTitle: An Automatic Alignment Bidirectional Visible Light Communication System Based on Red Laser Diode
abstract: In recent years, visible light communication using LEDs has attracted great attention. However, LED's narrow modulation bandwidth restricts the achievable data rate. In that case, researches on LD-based VLC are widely proceeding. Because of the high beam convergence of LDs, the terminal devices must be strictly aligned. In this paper, we propose an automatic alignment VLC system based on red LDs. By using the camera and the galvo, we demonstrate a mobile real-time VLC system over a distance of 0.6 meter and a field angle of ±10°. Based on the Gigabit Ethernet protocol, the system can provide a TCP data transmission of 909Mbps.

articleTitle: Information Processing Methods in Ergatic Robotic Systems
abstract: The report provides an overview of various methods and technologies for processing information received from sensors for robotic systems control. The issues of information integration for a robot when solving SLAM problems, navigation, and the priority tasks choice are considered; methods and algorithms for the man-robots interaction when using neuro-, myo-, oculos-interfaces, as well as information exchange using voice and gestures are distinguished. Information processing tasks are extended to cloud and fog computing. Examples are presented in various intefrfaces.

articleTitle: Composite Data Preparation Algorithm for SAR Imagery Object Recognition
abstract: The paper presents the approach to resolve the insufficient training data problem for object recognition on radar images. Article proposes the novel strategy of data preparation based on the fusion of objects and background images to form composite data. The composite samples were formed by the Poisson's image blending algorithm using open-source experimental database MSTAR and data synthesized by the pix2pix algorithm. It was shown that composite data is applicable in the conditions of a low number of initial data for training object detectors such as YOLOv5. According to mAP for the considered insufficient amount of training data case reaches 82%. It is shown that implementing training strategy based on the prepared composite dataset improves the accuracy recognition up to 3% of mAP. Generalization ability of trained detector was shown on delayed manually annotated samples from ICEYE database where model achieved mAP@0.5 of 62%.

articleTitle: New Clipping-and-Filtering Method for Peak-to-Average Power Ratio Reduction in OFDM
abstract: In this paper, the authors introduce a new clipping-and-filtering method for peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. The proposed algorithm aims to achieve four primary purposes. First, it eliminates the out-of-band frequency components of the clipping noise to avoid the adjacent channel leakage. Second, it constrains constellation distortion in a square-shaped region while maintaining certain distances among constellation points in the signal space. Third, it increases PAPR reduction performance. Fourth, it has low computational complexity. The experimental results on Matlab in DVB-T2 context for 16-QAM symbols are presented. Finally, a comparison of the PAPR reduction effectiveness of the proposed method with the constrained clipping method is given.

articleTitle: Statistical Correlations in Active Matter Based on Robotic Swarms
abstract: Robotic swarms are a promising tool for exploring the fundamental physics of active matter. In these designed systems, large assemblies of simple robots exhibit versatile dynamical behavior and a broad range of collective phenomena. However, extracting detailed statistical data for the behavior of large-scale robotic ensembles remains challenging due to the amount of measurements required and the need for computational resources for processing. In this paper, we introduce an experimental setup based on a robotic swarm complete with the necessary hardware and software platforms. Performing extensive experiments and extracting detailed kinematic information, we reveal a rich set of spatial correlations in stochastic robotic ensembles on the friction between individual robots and their packing density.

articleTitle: Technique for Suppressing Additive and Multiplicative Noises
abstract: To enhance noise immunity of the data transmission systems affected by additive and multiplicative noises it is suggested to perform pre-processing of the receiver input signal. Demonstrated below is the feasibility of both noise suppression technique and schematic diagram of a device implementing this technique.

articleTitle: The Transmission Test and Demonstration for 8K Ultra-high Definition TV Services Using DTMB-A
abstract: Digital terrestrial television multimedia broadcasting-advanced (DTMB-A) system has been officially adopted by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) as the latest international digital terrestrial television broadcasting (DTTB) standard in 2019. This paper introduces a live demonstration of 8K ultra-high definition (UHD) TV terrestrial broadcasting based on DTMB-A in Feb. 2021, China. The demonstration used the second-generation digital terrestrial television system C of the ITU-R BT. 1877 Recommendation, which supports a maximum payload rate of 200 Mbps by using channel bonding, code stream splitting and combing technologies. The system block diagram and the hardware devices of the trial are analysed technically in detail. The entire demonstration was conducted in Shenzhen Xinghe CoCo Park and displayed on its large outdoor UHD screen, which realized the first 8K live broadcast demonstration based on the DTMB-A in China.

articleTitle: Low Complexity DVB-S2X Frequency Synchronization for LEO Satellites
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of frequency synchronization for LEO satellite systems based on DVB-S2/S2X standard. This problem is rather crucial nowadays, since LEO satellite systems gain more and more popularity (e.g. Starlink) and at Low Earth Orbit the Doppler shift can change at a relatively high speed (tens of kHz per second). We demonstrate that the simple geostationary satellite synchronization algorithms, such as second-order PLL and the well-known Fitz algorithm, fail to solve this problem. We give recommendations on an efficient frequency synchronization systems design, which could solve the problem and keep the computational complexity of the entire scheme low at the same time.

articleTitle: Security of the Cryptosystem GPT Based on Rank Codes and Term-rank Codes
abstract: This paper investigates public key cryptosystems (PKC) in the rank metric and term-rank metric. For security analysis of cryptosystems, we introduce a GPT system. Recently, respective structural attacks this system were proposed by Over-beck. For GPT system, Overbeck's attack succeeds in polynomial time. We will discuss the new construction of Shiki system. This paper describes Overbeck's attack to the new Shiki system. Also, investigation of the possibility of using term-rank codes in public key cryptosystems.

articleTitle: Notes on the pursuit-evasion games between unmanned aerial vehicles operating in uncertain environments
abstract: We solve the planar case of the urgent pursuit-evasion problem for players using various strategies of motion. The following options are considered: players perform piecewise-linear motions; the pursuer moves in a straight line, and the evader moves in a circle; both players move along circular arcs. We propose schemes to solve the formulated problem based on the construction of Apollonius circles, which are geometric invariants. As participants of the game, we assume unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating in a non-deterministic environment. To solve the problem under uncertainty we use the theory of intelligent geometric control aimed at the joint application of complementary methods of precise geometric and flexible intelligent control as parts of one robotic system. Experimental studies of pursuit-evasion games are carried out in the MATLAB system using mathematical models of UAVs motion and wind loads.

articleTitle: Simplified Single-Scatter Path Loss Model of LED-based Non-Line-of-Sight Ultraviolet Communications
abstract: In this work, a simplified model of single-scatter path loss (PL) for the LED-based non-line-of-sight ultraviolet communication system is proposed. For the case of narrow field-of-view of receiver, a closed-form expression of PL is derived by modeling the LED emission pattern as Lambertian distribution. The proposed PL model is compared with the exact single-scatter PL model and the Monte Carlo numerical model to verify its effectiveness and accuracy. The results indicate that the root-mean-square-error between the proposed model and the exact single-scatter model is less than 0.5dB in its application ranges.

articleTitle: Shaping of Flat-Topped Element Patterns in Phased Arrays of Coupled Multimode Waveguides of Hexagonal Cross Section
abstract: Linear and planar phased array antennas of finite dimension with elements in the form of multimode waveguides of hexagonal cross-section coupled between each other via slots cut in their common walls are proposed and considered. Electrodynamical modeling including optimization of geometric parameters in order to shape flat-topped element patterns corresponding to the excitation of element input by waves of different polarization was carried out. The results characterizing the effectiveness of the approach are presented. The results obtained for planar phased arrays of finite dimension are compared with similar results obtained also for element patterns of infinite periodic phased arrays.

articleTitle: Scattering matrix simulation of broadband band-pass filter based on a multilayer technology
abstract: Application of multilayer technology based on a combination of strip and slot lines makes it possible to realize contactless transmission of a microwave signal between parts of a multilayer microwave devices. The advantages of this technology are shielding, small size characteristics and ease of manufacture. A significant limitation for the use of multilayer strip-slot technology in designing of broadband microwave devices is its narrow operating frequency band. The paper proposes a research of a broadband band-pass filter based on a multilayer strip-slot transition. According to the experimental data, the investigated broadband band-pass filter based on a multilayer strip-slot transition has a relative passband at a level of −3 dB relative to the maximum transmission coefficient equal to 49.5% (from 0.75 GHz to 1.243 GHz). In this case, the attenuation at the central frequency is 0.5 dB. The theoretical research carried out by 1) designing and modeling of an equivalent circuit of the broadband band-pass filter and 2) by its numerical modeling in ANSYS HFSS software. A model of the broadband band-pass filter manufactured and examined to confirm the results of the theoretical research. The results of an experimental study of the model of the broadband band-pass filter showed their correspondence to the results of theoretical modeling.

articleTitle: Multilayer Printed Radiator on Two Circular Polarizations for Wide-Angle Scanning Ka-band Tx/Rx Phased Array
abstract: A multilayer printed radiator for an active phased antenna array (APAA) of Ka-band satellite communications with switchable modes of operation for signal transmission and reception is considered. The design of the radiator is described and the results of calculations of the radiator model are presented. The radiator in the transmission mode (Tx) forms the field of the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), and in the reception mode - the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP). The radiator operates in the frequency range of 27-27.5 GHz and has a scanning area in the form of a cone with a solid angle of ±45 degrees. To reduce the level of cross-polarization, groups of four radiators with sequential rotation of 90 degrees are used. The results of calculations for such a group of radiators in the Floquet channel condition are presented.

articleTitle: Methods for Improving the Accuracy of Frequency Shift Estimation in 5G NR
abstract: Frequency synchronization is a necessary operation for all wireless communication systems. Due to the wide frequency range defined for 5G NR systems, this procedure becomes critical. To ensure high transmission rates and the use of high-order modulation, up to 256 QAM for 5G communication systems, it is necessary to ensure high frequency synchronization accuracy. In this article, we have reviewed various approaches to implementing frequency synchronization and proposed, in our opinion, the most effective method for correcting the frequency shift of the signal.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Interleaved Partition-based PTS with Low Complexity
abstract: In this paper, first, the authors evaluate the efficiency of algorithms for the interleaved partition-based PTS (Partial Transmit Sequence) scheme using only a small-sized single inverse fast Fourier transform block and a binary phase sequence. Then we implement practical hardware for this PTS scheme. The hardware architecture is conducted on FPGA using the 16-bit fixed-point representation. Simulation and FPGA experimental results indicate that peak-to-average-power ratio reduction efficiency of our scheme for DVB-T2 system is almost as high as in the traditional PTS (T-PTS), and its computational complication is significantly lower.

articleTitle: Enabling Synchronous Uplink NOMA in Wi-Fi Networks
abstract: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is a promising technology for future Wi-Fi, In uplink NOMA, stations with different channel conditions transmit simultaneously at the same frequency by splitting the signal by power level. Since Wi-Fi uses random access, the implementation of uplink NOMA in Wi-Fi faces many challenges. The paper presents a data transmission mechanism in Wi-Fi networks that enables synchronous uplink NOMA, where multiple stations start data transmission to the access point simultaneously. The developed mechanism can work with the legacy Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) mechanism in Wi-Fi. With simulation, it is shown that the developed mechanism can double the total throughput and geometric mean throughput compared with the legacy EDCA.

articleTitle: Specifics of Communication Organization and Attacks on Medical Cyber-physical Devices
abstract: The computerization of medicine opens up wide opportunities not only for providing assistance, but also for intruders. The violation of digital control of medical devices can lead not only to data leakage, but also to a threat to human health and life. The diversity and specificity of medical cyber-physical devices makes it difficult to protect them and consider the threat landscape. The purpose of this work is to systematize attacks on medical systems. The authors highlight the features of medical cyber-physical systems (MCPS), consider a set of typical attacks. The authors have identified both common attacks for various CPS, and specialized attacks aimed at medical devices and systems. The paper analyzes the existing systematization as well. The authors present a developed new systematization of attacks on a wide range of features, which is distinguished by the completeness and highlighting of all important attack aspects from the point of view of the medical field.

articleTitle: The Fast CU Splitting Method Based on CU Size, Quantization Parameters and Difference of Variances
abstract: HEVC is one of the most efficient video-coding standards used in different kinds of services. In current HEVC model there is a large number of methods for encoding: different modes and various kinds of frame structures. In a default algorithm the full search of different encoding combinations to find the most efficient one is realized. It leads to high encoding complexity of the standard implementation. To reduce the complexity of encoding algorithm the method for fast CU (Coding Unit) decision is offered in this paper. It is based on picture structure, quantization parameter and size of CTB (Coding Tree Block). The experimental results showed that this method gives about 43% of time reduction with about 1% of coding efficiency loss.

articleTitle: A Modification of the Hybrid Projection Method for Analysis of Doubly Periodic Structures with Inhomogeneous Magneto-Dielectric Elements
abstract: We consider the problem of plane electromagnetic wave scattering on two-dimensional periodic structures composed of magneto-dielectric elements, which are inhomogeneous in both longitudinal and transverse directions and arranged on a homogeneous magneto-dielectric substrate. A modification of the hybrid projection method is developed for numerical analysis of the structure with accounting for the feature of the elements of the latter. The method includes projection of the Maxwell equations for the fields in the structure on transverse vector orthonormal functions, projection matching of the fields on the boundaries of the region containing the elements of the structure, and application of one-dimensional finite-element method reducing the problem to a system of linear algebraic equations.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Reflector Antenna with Wide Angle Mechanical Beam Scanning
abstract: The millimeter wave dual-reflector antenna for low Earth orbit (LEO) communication satellite providing the beam scanning within hemispherical sector by rotations of reflector and subreflector is under consideration. The results of optimization of the antenna geometry and feed horn characteristics which provide the antenna high gain and low side lobe level in the whole scanning sector are presented.

articleTitle: Style transfer in NLP: a framework and multilingual analysis with Friends TV series
abstract: Style transfer is an important and a rapidly developing of Natural Language Processing. This days more and more methods and models are proposed which allow us to generate text in predefined style. In this paper we propose a framework for style transfer of “Friends” TV series. The trained models are able to mimic one of 6 main characters of this famous TV-series in English and Russian. We also present a dialogue dataset of “Friends” subtitles in English and its Russian automatic translation. In addition to that we perform a multilingual comparison of “Friends” style transfer in the two considered languages.

articleTitle: Applying Convolutional Neural Networks for Security in VANET
abstract: This article discusses the problem of identifying attacks in the VANET using convolutional neural networks. The main idea of this work is to study the effectiveness of applying deep learning models 1D and 2D Convolutional Neural Network to detect attacks in the VANET. The analysis of the effectiveness of the considered machine learning models was carried out on synthetically generated data of the VANET network segment with three types of DDoS attacks. In addition, the results obtained are compared with the common ensemble methods CatBoost and XGBoost. Computational experiments have shown that in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score metrics, the CNN 1D deep learning model is the most effective model for identifying attacks in VANET networks and has an accuracy of 89.081%. The considered structures of convolutional neural networks surpassed the results of ensemble methods by an average of 9.518%.

articleTitle: Optimization of the prediction of the near-Earth space objects trajectory by interpolation of gravitational pulling force and atmospheric density
abstract: The problem of the high-cost process of calculating the Earth's gravitational pulling force and the force of atmospheric resistance in predicting the trajectories of near-Earth space objects is considered. To solve this problem, an interpolation model is proposed that allows speeding up the process of calculating of the mentioned forces with insignificant losses in the accuracy of computations.

articleTitle: Elbrus-2C3: a Dual-Core VLIW Processor with Integrated Graphics
abstract: Elbrus 2000 (E2K) is an advanced general-purpose VLIW architecture featuring patented technologies of secure program execution and offering x86 compatibility via dynamic binary translation. This paper introduces the sixth generation of E2K architecture and describes a 2 GHz dual-core processor with integrated PowerVR GX6650 graphics based on it, planned for mass production in 2022 using 16 nm FinFET technology and aimed at the use in embedded and wearable systems, portable computers, thin clients and tablets. Key processor specifications are summarized, and its design, including E2K version 6 cores, integrated graphics and codecs, DDR4 memory and I/O controllers, and on-chip interconnection network, is described. A COM Express Type 6 module with this processor, enabling compatibility with different form factors, is presented.

articleTitle: Accelerating Extreme Search Based on Natural Gradient Descent with Beta Distribution
abstract: Natural gradient descent is an optimization method developed from the information geometry. It works well for many applications due to the better convergence and can be a good alternative for gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent in machine learning and statistics. The goal of this work is to propose a natural gradient descent algorithm with the beta distribution and the stepsize adaptation. We compare the minimizing process of gradient descent with natural gradient descent with respect to Gauss and Beta distributions. Additionally, the calculating of the Fisher matrix for computing natural gradient will be represented.

articleTitle: An integrated indoor VLC+PLC system for video broadcast and positioning
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) technology can simultaneously support voice, video broadcast, indoor positioning, and other value-added services. In this paper, Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are used to transmit multiple high definition television programs with the combination of VLC as the access point and power line communication (PLC) as the network backbone to avoid the sophisticated networking issue. The positioning function was also implemented into this integrated VLC+PLC system by generate unique identification label sequences through Manchester coding for each LED, using on-off keying to modulate light to send label beacons, and utilizing photo-diode to receive it. Since the label information of the reference point is associated with each LED's location and stored in the server database using passive positioning as an example, when the target point is within the communication range of a reference point, it will receive the optical signal transmitted by this particular reference point and the target point can be located by the server. The video broadcast service and the indoor label positioning within VLC+PLC system are independent services needing different transmission schemes [1]. In this paper, a novel scheme is proposed to integrate the video broadcast service and indoor label positioning into one LED, which can support these two services at the same time.

articleTitle: A Deep Neural Network Architecture for Solving Classification Problems on Multidimensional Time Series of Financial Markets
abstract: The paper describes the results of a study of existing architectures of deep neural networks designed to solve classification problems. Multidimensional time series of financial markets are used as data. The problems of binary and multiclass classification are considered. Fully connected, recurrent (LSTM) and hybrid combined architectures of neural networks are analyzed as tools. The studied multidimensional time series is obtained by combining one-dimensional time series of the asset value, trading volume, technical indicators, as well as some other parameters.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Reputation Model for Secure Routing Based on the OLSR Protocol
abstract: The paper proposes a modification of the OLSR routing protocol in order to improve the security of routing in a self-organizing network. To provide security, a new reputation model was presented and implemented. The model allows nodes to determine local values of communication links’ reputation in the network using test packets, as well as exchange recommendations with other nodes on the network. The global reputation of communication links is determined as a result of recommendations aggregation. The computation of the routing table is based on the global reputation using the algorithm proposed in our previous paper. We proposed some changes in the tables and messages of the OLSR protocol to implement the presented model. The effectiveness of the proposed solutions is demonstrated by an example.

articleTitle: Signalization of objects on the sonar images using neural network segmentation methods
abstract: This paper is devoted to the development of neural network algorithms of segmentation for automatic analysis of sonar images. Object signaling, low-quality areas detection, and seabed line extraction tasks are determined. A brief analysis of the sonar images is presented. The method and results of preparing training samples set of less than 1000 sonar images are described. An algorithm based on neural network segmentation is proposed. Correct object signaling probability 86.92 % with false signaling probability 23.03 % is achieved, the accuracy of bottom line extraction reaches 97.71 %. The lack of data for the correct solution of the problem of low-quality areas extraction is shown. Parameters of the hardware-software module for real-time processing are given.

articleTitle: The Perspective of SAR Satellite Application for ISS Imaging
abstract: The paper argues that inverse synthetic aperture synthesis technology can be applied to carry out the Earth remote sensing satellites (ERS) adaptation for the International Space Station (ISS) image receiving. Based on the existing model in 3D-MAX and ISS trajectory, we calculated ISS radar projection. Our model produced the radio hologram, which was formed as an array of single signals reflected from the station surface. As a result, the bright inverse SAR image of the ISS was achieved. It can be used as a visual demonstration of the ERS system operation.

articleTitle: A two-frequency compact klystron three-gap resonator with a suspended dielectric substrate
abstract: This article presents the design of a two-frequency small-sized three-gap rectangular resonator with a suspended dielectric substrate for a low-voltage amplifying klystron C and X wavelength range. Its main electrodynamic and electronic parameters were calculated for anti-phased (4.7 GHz) and in-phased (9.67 GHz) modes of oscillation. The analysis of the HF electric field along the interaction space was carried out for each of the modes. The three-gap rectangular resonator can be tuned to multiples resonant frequency, which makes it possible to operate as a frequency multiplier. Electronic parameters were calculated for the frequency multiplicity mode also. Calculations show the possibility of obtaining an output power of about 1 kW in a klystron with this resonator at an efficiency of about 60% and an accelerating voltage of 2.6 kV. The three-gap resonator can be used in miniature multi-beam centimeter and millimeter-wave klystrons operating in the mode of an amplifier or frequency multiplier.

articleTitle: Permittivity Measurement for Powder Materials Using a Volumetric Strip-slot Junction
abstract: Permittivity measurements of radar-absorbing materials in a wide band remain an urgent task. Despite the fact that there are known methods for measuring materials in the form of plates, measuring the properties of powder materials remains poorly studied. The paper presents the results of studies of a prototype meter in the form of a volumetric strip-slot junction, implemented using a volumetric-modular method.

articleTitle: Development and Research of a Deep Neural Network Architecture for Solving Regression Problems on Multidimensional Time Series of Financial Markets
abstract: This paper describes the results of a study of solving the regression problem using machine learning technologies. In particular, fully connected and hybrid models were used for this. Multidimensional time series of financial markets are used as data. One of the areas of application of this research is the analysis and forecasting of time series of financial markets.

articleTitle: Forecasting in Financial Markets Using the ADAM Architecture and Reinforcement Learning Methods
abstract: This paper describes the results of using the ADAM (Adaptive Deep Autonomous Machine) architecture in the task of predicting movements in financial markets. In addition, the data transform algorithm has been developed that converts their distribution over each of the coordinates similar to a uniform one.

articleTitle: Software and Methodological Toolkit for the Design and Development of Technical Devices in the Model-Based Systems Engineering Paradigm
abstract: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and its' tool the Systems Modelling Language (SysML) are recognized to serve as the fundament for design and development (D&D) of system models and digital twins. But the existing MBSE software (SW) tools based on SysML are complex and expensive. The paper raises the question: “Is it possible to make usage of MBSE software and methodological tools during space instruments design and development (SIDD) available to a wide audience of potential users?” To answer this question, for SIDD lifecycle phases (LPs) were developed methodological tools (MTs) based on improvements of such MBSE tools as Quality Function Deployment (QFD), House of Quality (HoQ); SysML, and their synthesis with systems engineering (SE) tools. MTs were implemented in the widely available SW tools. Proposed MTs allow to reduce time required for SysML requirements diagram development and update from several days to minutes; for LPs realization from 5 to 10%.

articleTitle: A Method of Auxiliary Surface Currents in 2D Problems of Electromagnetic Scattering by Penetrable Cylinders
abstract: A new modification of the method of integral equations is proposed for solution of two-dimensional problems of electromagnetic wave scattering by a homogeneous penetrable cylinder of arbitrary cross section. The modification includes approximation of the specified contour of the cross section by a polygon, use of auxiliary surface currents uniformly distributed on each side of the polygon, and satisfaction of the boundary conditions for the tangential fields in the collocation points arranged in the midpoints of the polygon sides. Analytic expressions are derived for matrix elements of the system of equations obtained as a result of algebraization. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated in a few examples of wave scattering by cylinders of circular and square cross-section.

articleTitle: Height Estimation of Atmospheric Reentry of Vehicle Tracked With LFM Waveforms
abstract: Conditions for the moment of atmospheric reentry of vehicles tracked with chirp radar are studied in this paper. A Kalman filter is applied to estimate the position, velocity and acceleration of the vehicle moving from above the atmosphere and through the atmosphere. While the vehicle moves above the atmosphere the Kalman filter calculates estimates of position and velocity. Detecting the moment of atmospheric reentry is obtained with taking into account a residual which is equal to a difference between measurement of range and predicted range. This residual is used to estimate the height of atmospheric reentry.

articleTitle: A Scheme of Visible Light Indoor Positioning Based on Image Communication
abstract: In response to the ever-increasing demand for indoor positioning, this paper proposes an imaging positioning system based on visible light communication with advantages of strong versatility, low cost, high precision, and easy for deployment, and it meets the Chinese national standard GB/T36628 ‘Information technology - Telecommunications and information exchange between systems - Visible light communication - Part4: Transmission protocol for indoor positioning’. Under the practical system setup of the light and also the distance between the LED lamp and the intelligent device, the system performance has been tested with the satisfactory accuracy and processing speed.

articleTitle: Guest System Call Execution by the Application Level Binary Compiler x86-Elbrus
abstract: Expanding the amount of application available for a not widespread hardware platform is a very crucial but not an easy task. One of the ways to solve it is to use the binary translation technology, which translates codes of one architecture into the codes of another. In this article we will consider the x86-Elbrus application level binary compiler, in particular, the mechanism for processing system calls in it, because system calls nowadays are the integral part of almost any application. As the result of this work, optimizations of application binary compiler, which aim to speed up system calls processing will be presented and graphs will be provided that demonstrate the relevance of the proposed optimizations.

articleTitle: Features of Calibration of Large Stationary Phased Array Antennas
abstract: Some aspects of calibration of large stationary phased array antennas are considered. It is shown, that, when calibrating a large array outside the anechoic chamber, there are the problems associated with reflections of the signal from the ground and with incorrect determination of the position of the source antenna. This leads to beam pattern distortion after calibration and beam forming. To reduce distortion, source antenna should be placed properly. Several antenna sources in different positions can also be used to reduce distortion.

articleTitle: Beam-Domain Interference Mitigation System Concept in Application to Automotive Radar
abstract: The present paper is focused on “on-board” Anti-Interference signal processing for 77 GHz automotive radar with antenna array. Interference Mitigation System (IMS) based on two-steps beam-domain approach is proposed. The core of the system is combination of adaptive beanforming and additional subtraction algorithm in frequency domain. Verification of proposed IMS concept characteristics was performed by MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Research of Financial Time-series Statistical Properties
abstract: This paper describes the results of research of the stock charts of the cost and trading volume of companies. This task has been reduced to the analysis of statistical properties of time series.

articleTitle: High-performance software for memristor-based neural network simulation and optimization
abstract: This work is devoted to the creation of high-speed software for simulation of artificial neural networks based on memristors (ANNM). Simulation modeling is the main tool for optimizing the parameters of the systems under development, while it requires significant computing resources. In this paper, software is proposed that uses the maximum available computer resources, which makes it possible to speed up the process of modeling and optimize the accuracy, fault tolerance and reliability of ANNM by several times.

articleTitle: Modelling of a Small-Sized Waveguide Radiator with Elliptical Polarization
abstract: Waveguide and horn antennas with elliptical polarization of the radiation field are extensively applied in radio detection and location, satellite communication, and other branches of radio engineering. Because of their high reliability, electric strength and technological effectiveness, such antennas are promising for use in onboard radio systems. However, in practical application of antennas, there are common restrictions as regards their overall longitudinal dimensions. In view of this, the principal task is to reduce longitudinal dimensions while maintaining frequency and polarization characteristics of the antennas. This research paper discusses a waveguide radiator on the basis of a polarizer with an integrated slow-wave structure in the form of a linear partition and two protrusions. Design parameters, frequency and polarization characteristics are given. Possibility to reduce overall longitudinal dimensions twofold, when compared with the existing analogues, is suggested. Directional characteristics for the working band-width of 8-8.5 GHz are addressed.

articleTitle: Simple Polynomial Windows for Spectral Analysis of Signals That Minimize the Spectrum Sidelobe Level on a Segment of the Frequency Axis
abstract: A synthesis problem is solved for low-order polynomial windows that are optimal by the criterion of minimizing the highest sidelobe level on a given segment of the frequency axis. The windows feature an arbitrary specified sidelobe falloff rate, a simple calculation algorithm and are intended for embedded real-time systems. It is shown that reduction of the length of the minimization segment significantly improves the main window characteristics. Windows are synthesized with different sidelobe falloff rates, their parameters are provided, and characteristics are analyzed.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Comparison of the OFDM and FBMC Modulations for Wi-Fi 7 in the Presence of the Complex Nakagami-m Fading
abstract: The research studies the comparison of the performance of the Wi-Fi 7 systems employing either orthogonal multiple access (OMA - OFDM) or non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA - FBMC/OQAM) technologies in presence of multipath fading described by the complex Nakagami-m model. The performance was characterized by energy efficiency. An analysis of the impact of channel parameters (i.e. the amount of fading and average fading power) and modulation parameters (constellation size of the quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) and the number of subcarriers) was made. Along with lower-order modulations, the performed research assumed the largest possible constellation - 4k-QAM.

articleTitle: Efficient Hardware-Agnostic DBMS Operator Implementation Using SYCL
abstract: Heterogeneous hardware requires tedious optimization of DBMS algorithms for each platform it supports when implemented with vendor-specific toolchains. Such an approach inevitably leads to specialization and maintainability issues. In this paper we evaluate several hash-joins implemented with a high-level language SYCL and compare the data across different execution devices. We provide a roof-line performance estimations for algorithms and show these implementations are on par with existing hardware specific implementations.

articleTitle: Nonlinear MIMO receiver with low complexity
abstract: There are two types of signal reception algorithms. Nonlinear methods have a better performance than linear ones, but they also have greater computational complexity. This paper will consider an algorithm that can reduce complexity with an acceptable reduction in efficiency. The Maximum Likelihood algorithm shows less error than other receivers, but at the same time it has huge computational complexity. This can be explained by the fact that the algorithm enumerates all possible signal variants and selects the best one among them. Its complexity increases exponentially. The Sphere Decoder was created as an optimization of the Maximum Likelihood algorithm. The algorithm considers not all variants of the transmitted signal, but only those that lie inside a hypersphere. A new task arises - the selection of the correct radius. The radius should not be too small, otherwise the correct node may not fall inside the sphere and should not be too large, otherwise the complexity increases greatly. Calculating the radius requires additional computing power. In this paper, a new variation of a Sphere Decoder with low computational complexity will be presented

articleTitle: Development and research of algorithms for recognition of breast diseases by mammographic images using neural networks
abstract: Diseases of the mammary glands rank first among the diseases of the female population. This work is devoted to the development of an algorithm for the diagnosis of breast diseases by mammographic images using neural networks. The article presents the result of choosing the optimal parameters of an artificial neural network trained to solve the problem of classifying breast diseases by mammograms based on Haralic's textural features.

articleTitle: Algorithm of risk assessment in the task of identifying destructive content in social networks
abstract: This paper introduces the algorithm of the risk assessment system in terms of sending messages in a social network (both within the personal correspondence of two users, and when publishing a message for an arbitrary number of users that are part of a community or a group). Such a system can be embedded in a common framework for identifying and blocking destructive content in social media. The work presents a model of interaction of actors when sending a message, and describes the approach to solving the problem of multi-criteria risk assessment of transferring the destructive content based, as well as forming the corresponding discrete value scales and specified convolution matrices. The use of such system allows efficient management of the resources of the social network hardware through a priori simplified procedure of content verification, while in-depth (or enhanced) verification of the contents (or its transmission to a moderator) is only carried out if the value of the integral risk coefficient exceeds the specified threshold. The proposed risk assessment system can be used both for real-time verification of messages sent, on request of the moderator, or on-demand (if there are complaints from the users). The paper contains the simulation results of the work of the proposed algorithm in the MATLAB environment for different numbers of recipients of the message, values of content destructiveness, and sender trust coefficients.

articleTitle: Analytical Description of Chaotic Radio Pulse Receiver
abstract: Analytical model of energy receiver of ultra-wideband chaotic radio pulses with large processing gain is derived and investigated.

articleTitle: Trust model, reliability theory in theory of secrecy
abstract: This article presents the results of the application of reliability theory in the theory of secrecy systems. The possibility of assessing the persistence of cryptographic systems in time is shown taking into account the probability of compromising the computer by a cryptanalyst, failure of hardware components of the computer.

articleTitle: A Diagram-Forming Scheme Implemented According to the Butler Matrix Scheme
abstract: The work is aimed at describing a compact Butler matrix that allows forming independent rays in a radiation pattern. Such a matrix is a set of directional couplers, phase shifters and crossovers. These devices are connected to the frequency at which they operate, so at low frequencies they will take up a lot of space on the printed circuit board. In our work, we studied the option of replacing microstrip segments with structures with equivalent characteristics. Such manipulations with the Butler matrix allowed to reduce its area by 80% in relation to the standard design.

articleTitle: Applicability of the kNN Algorithm in the Problem of Pattern Classification on Time Series of Financial Markets
abstract: This paper describes an environment for learning with reinforcement of deep neural networks and an optimized kNN algorithm. The results of the study of models combined into an ensemble trained using this algorithm are presented.

articleTitle: Satellite Radio Monitoring Stations Observation Planning: Time Alignment Observation Algorithm
abstract: The rapid development of satellites constellations in low orbits lead to the increase in the number of spacecrafts. Thus, the problem arises of optimizing the planning of observations by ground stations. The mechanism of plan optimization is presented, the quality criterion is introduced, taking into account the total observation time of the spacecraft and the deviation of each spacecraft time from the mean value. A number of planning algorithms have been analyzed and modeled using the orbital data of operating spacecrafts. The results show the high quality of proposed method.

articleTitle: On the Concatenated Code Construction for Slotted Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access
abstract: A novel code construction applied to an especial class of non-orthogonal multiple access system over vector-disjunctive channel in which users send some information vectors of bits with particular length is regarded by us. We suggest specific encoding and decoding schemes suitable for these transmission cases. Coding algorithm is represented by concatenated code construction with a combination of interleaved BCH code and finite geometry (Steiner triple systems). We show some simulation results for frame error rate (FER) and for relative sum-rate of our structure in the case of varied number of active users and various coding schemes. These simulation results demonstrate a good performance in non-orthogonal multiple access system thanks to using specific code construction.

articleTitle: Block Structure of the Mathematical Models of Dipole Arrays
abstract: Blocks of functional matrix for modeling the electromagnetic fields of antenna array and closely located scattering objects are determined. Asymptotic correspondence of 2D and 3D antenna theory problems based on nontrivial formulation of the Lorentz lemma is considered. Mathematical model that includes phased array and scattering objects is formulated as a system of the integral equations. The structure of the general functional matrix for various variants of scattering objects is developed. Block operators agree well with the numerical method of moments. Dynamic pattern as set of values of the electromagnetic field for a given direction is determined. An important for practical application case of scattering objects as perfect conductive cylinders and non-uniform dielectric objects is considered. The obtained results for dynamic patterns of scan phased array can be used to correct the initial phase distribution of the array.

articleTitle: On the Efficiency of Combinatorial Generation for Adaptive Image Steganography
abstract: Steganographic embedding is an effective method of protecting information transmitted over an open communication channel. Steganography techniques hide information in digital objects by embedding to make it invisible to an attacker. The most common covers for hiding additional information are multimedia data, in particular digital images. The embedding effectiveness is mainly assessed by the criteria of invisibility and capacity. One of the ways to improve the embedding efficiency is to choose the best location of message bits within the cover object, but it usually takes a long time to iterate through a large number of such embedding options. In this paper, we propose a new approach to finding the best option for steganographic embedding of information into the phase spectrum of the discrete Fourier transform based on the methods of combinatorial generation. The results of the experiments show that the new approach allows us to reduce the best embedding option search time, while the invisibility and capacity indicators remain high.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Classical and Bipolar Morphological Models for Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: The paper is dedicated to the convolutional neural networks hardware solutions and their implementation. We describe the hardware modules developed, which are specialized in processing of classical and bipolar morphological models of neural networks.

articleTitle: Double-Gap Klystron Photonic Crystal Resonator with Stripe Lines on a Dielectric Substrate
abstract: The article presents the results of numerical simulation of a new design of a double-gap photonic crystal resonator (DGPBG) for use in a multi-beam low-voltage Ku band klystron. A design feature is the use of a photonic crystal lattice and a dielectric substrate with strip resonant elements in the resonator. The main electrodynamic parameters were investigated for the main anti-phase and higher in-phase modes of oscillations. The spectrum of resonant frequencies of the resonator is analyzed in the range from 10 to 21 GHz. The electronic parameters were investigated in the range of accelerating voltages from 2.5 to 7.5 kV. Practical recommendations have been developed for the selection of optimal parameters of resonator designs, which can be used in the development of miniature multi-beam klystron-type devices operating as amplifiers and generators.

articleTitle: Spatial-Consistently Shifted Antenna Methodology for DAS Modeling in NR V2X Applications
abstract: This paper considers the problem of distributed antenna systems modeling (DAS) for NR V2X applications. The principal difference between co-located (CAS) and distributed antenna systems is distinguished. Spatial-consistently shifted antenna methodology is proposed for DAS modeling. This approach is based on 3GPP TR 38.901 spatial consistency procedure and can be used for V2V and V2B links simulations as an enhancement of the conventional methodology

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Nano Scale FIN FET Using Silvaco TCAD
abstract: We present design and simulation of a single gate Fin-FET structure on the SOI substrate using Silvaco TCAD. A 45 nm channel length Fin-FET structure is compared with conventional MOSFET structure having same channel length. Different structural and process parameters such as length, width, height, dielectric thickness, doping etc has been optimized for designing the Fin-FET. The simulated structure shows the threshold voltage of 0.37643, lower DIBL, higher drain saturation current and improved parameters as compared to the conventional MOSFET structure.

articleTitle: Code-Domain NOMA Solutions for Wireless Uplink
abstract: In this review paper, we consider the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) schemes for wireless uplink. We assume an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) multiple access channel (MAC). We start with the capacity region, followed by the practical proposals for 5G cellular systems. We also consider code-division multiple-access (CDMA) schemes with a random spreading sequence as a predecessor of non-orthogonal multiple access. As a final step, we compare several practical solutions with the use of Polar and LDPC codes. We found the NOMA schemes to achieve better energy efficiency than orthogonal transmission schemes under the same modulation, thanks to a good performance of polar codes under a short block length.

articleTitle: Some Features of Generalized Mikaelian Lens with Negative Refractive Index
abstract: A flat transversely inhomogeneous dielectric lens with focus located at some specified distance from its surface is known as generalized Mikaelian lens. In the present work, a further generalization of the indicated lens on the case of using a material with negative refractive index in its design is considered. A new formula is derived for describing the profile of the negative refractive index. Some numerical results characterizing wave focusing by the indicated lens are presented and comparison of them with similar results obtained for the lens of the same dimensions but with positive refractive index is carried out.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Efficiency of Radar Target Classification by Heinen Polarization Parameters in the Monostatic Configuration
abstract: A mathematical model of the radar target classification based on Heinen polarization parameters was developed. Simulations of the functioning process was carried out to analyze the effectiveness of the developed model. Based on these simulation results, an analysis of the effectiveness of this group of polarization parameters for the radar target classification problem was carried out. The article presents some results of the simulation.

articleTitle: Embedded Online Machine Learning
abstract: The paper presents research on a set of “classical” machine learning algorithms for tiny (microbatch, i.e., batch size equal to or less than 128) embedded online machine learning on ARM processor boards with hard memory limits and a tiny memory footprint while running on a single CPU without multithreading. We propose mathematical improvements to algorithms as well as other programming optimizations. In the presence of evolving data streams, we present an adaptation of the Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) learning algorithm for classification tasks, the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost, XGB) and the Random Forest (RF) learning algorithms for supervised anomaly detection tasks, and the Extended Isolation Forest (EIF) learning algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection tasks. In this scenario, as new data is added over time, the connection between the class and the characteristics may shift, resulting in concept drift. The proposed technique generates new members of the ensemble from microbatches and/or batches of data for each algorithm as new data becomes available. The maximum ensemble size is specified, but learning does not stop when it reaches this size because the ensemble is constantly updated with new data to ensure compatibility with the current notion. We tested our technique on real-world data and compared it to the original batch-incremental learning algorithms for data streams. Our implementations gain a speedup in inference up to several times even demonstrating prediction quality improvement by 0.1-0.3 in terms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${F_{1}}$</tex> measure in some cases.

articleTitle: Microstrip High Bandwidth Directional Couplers with Reduced Area
abstract: Designs of compact couplers with four and five plug-in stubs with operating frequencies of 1 GHz are presented. The use of idle loops together with high-resistance sections made it possible to reduce the dimensions of such devices by 70.7% and 68.45%, respectively. The miniaturization process is supposed to produce compact structures with equivalent characteristics for quarter-wave sections. The combination of line bends, arrangement of elements in free areas of the device and idle loops can significantly reduce the dimensions of directional couplers with insignificant degradation in performance. Compact and standard designs were developed for one and the same frequency and substrate parameters, which allows them to be compared correctly. Unfortunately, the size of the devices was reduced with the deterioration of the characteristics of the frequency-dependent devices.

articleTitle: Xtext Grammar of Driver Logical Condition Factor
abstract: Studies have shown significant benefits of the use of Domain Specific Languages (DSL). However, designing a DSL still seems to be an art, rather than a craft following a clear methodology. It is a hard task to design and implement traffic flow simulators with minimum difficulty. Numerous factors contribute to urban roadways traffic flow problems including weather factors, road factors, human factors, and so on. It is valued to design a single modeling tool for tracing the influences. This paper presents a DSL Xtext grammar of the driver logical condition model, which is one of the entire framework models designed for modeling traffic flow factors.

articleTitle: The Model of Conjoint Servicing of Real Time and Elastic Traffic Streams Through Processor Sharing (PS) Discipline with Access Control
abstract: Over the recent years our communicating networks have witnessed huge upsurge in the capacities and diversities of the data gathered over the Internet of Things (IoT) and other massive applications. The management of such huge volumes of data is proving to be very challenging and networking industry is looking for the solutions to deal with such scenarios as the networks are being upgraded from 4G to 5G communication systems. A major proportion of this data traffic contains complex, non-structured and miscellaneous data referred as “Big Data”, mostly evolving from smart networks. Though 5G proposes guidelines to handle massive data and resource management but there are no proper methods to implement efficient resource allocation and management especially in a multiservice shared network. Such shared networks are very promising to support smart networking environments and IoT as they deal with heterogenous data streams (such as LTE, NB-IoT etc.) originating from varied sources. Keeping this challenge in mind we have designed a framework for multiservice access node of the 5G mobile communication network, that provides a procedure for efficient resource sharing between two traffic streams (real-time and elastic data services) based on the use of the PS (Processor Sharing) discipline and access restrictions for each of the jointly serviced streams. The constructed model can be used to estimate the volume of the resource during the joint transmission of traffic of modern communication applications that provide the specified QoS indicators. Additionally, access control allows to define conditions for a differentiated servicing and assign priorities to the traffic streams.

articleTitle: Memory transformer with hierarchical attention for long document processing
abstract: Transformers have attracted lots of interest from the researchers. Up to now, transformers achieved state-of-the-art results in a wide range of natural language processing tasks such as different sequence modeling tasks like language understanding, text summarization and translation, and definitely more transformers to come. Still, transformers has their limitations in the tasks requiring long document processing. This paper introduces a new version of transformer, a Sentence level transformer with global memory pooling and hierarchical attention to cope with long text. We replace self-attention of vanilla transformer with multi-head attention between memory and a sequence, and also add a decoder sequence selector on the top of the encoder output. In our architecture sentences are encoded in parallel and then summarized with soft-attention on every decoding step. Proposed model was validated in machine translation task. We hypothesize that attaching memory slots to each sequence improves the quality of translation, besides tuning the model on context-aware data set by using pre-trained sequence-level weights will help to get more precise translation and promote translating long documents. Results show that extending each sentence with a memory slot and employing the attention over the encoder outputs improves translation results.

articleTitle: Are Neural Networks the Best Way for Encrypted Traffic Classification?
abstract: Are Neural Networks the best way for encrypted traffic classification? — Currently, the answer is “no”. In the future, maybe, however, much more research is needed to achieve the goal. Many recent papers study how to apply neural networks for traffic classification. Although the accuracy of the best machine learning algorithms is well below 100%, they work surprisingly well, even for encrypted traffic. This paper looks deep inside the encrypted traffic of widely used applications and points out the essential peculiarities of the security protocols. The paper reveals that the abilities of the neural networks to classify encrypted traffic are solidly limited by the amount of exposed unencrypted data. Without it, the algorithms classify traffic randomly. The paper identifies the plain-text data in the encrypted traffic that hints to the neural network algorithms. Based on the findings, the paper describes a spot-on, lightweight, and learning-free method that can easily classify the traffic encrypted with current security protocols. Finally, the paper predicts that the next versions of security protocols may conceal more data and complicate traffic classification. So, the paper analyzes the recently proposed amendments to the encryption protocols and their influence on the performance of the existing traffic classification algorithms.

articleTitle: Performance Impact of Error Correction Codes in RNS with Returning Methods and Base Extension
abstract: In this paper, we study techniques of correction codes for systems based on the Residue Number System (RNS). Self-correcting and error detection are important properties of RNS that allow the development of distributed data storage systems. However, the complexity of several approaches have a significant influence on system performance, it mostly depends on two methods: expanding the number base in the residual class and converting numbers from the residual system to the positional system. In this work, we review the state-of-the-art methods in the field and show that the most efficient error correction method combines the syndrome method and our method to expand the number base.

articleTitle: Intelligent Module for System Trading of Financial Markets Assets Based on an Ensemble of Deep Neural Networks and the DQN Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper describes an environment for reinforcement learning of deep neural networks and a classical optimized DQN algorithm with two models and a buffer. Multidimensional time series of financial markets are used as data. The results of the study of models combined into an ensemble trained using this algorithm are presented.

articleTitle: Data Association for Multi-Object Tracking Using Assignment Algorithms
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) plays a very important role in advanced applications such as driver assistance systems, autonomous vehicles, aircraft monitoring systems. One of the fundamental problems of multi-object tracking is the unknown data association. At each time step, we get multiple sensor measurements. However, we don't know where these sensor measurements come from. Each measurement can come from one of the objects detected in the previous time step, from a new object entering the field of view (FOV), or from clutter. As the number of objects and measurements increases, the combinatorial nature causes the number of data association hypotheses to increase rapidly, making it impossible to consider all data associations [1,2]. One approach to solving the data association problem is to transform it into an optimal assignment problem. One approach to solving the data association problem is to use algorithms of the optimal assignment problem. In this paper, we will introduce the method of using optimal assignment algorithms to solve the data association problem in MOT. At the same time, we also compare the performance of these algorithms in terms of data association accuracy and computational complexity. The results showed that using assignment algorithms like Gibbs sampling brings high performance in data association.

articleTitle: Scheduling algorithms in cellular MIMO systems
abstract: In this work, we study the resource allocation problem for downlink in 5G New Radio (NR) mobile networks in the case of orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA). One of the key features of 5G mobile networks is the usage of antenna arrays that allows them to form beams in a specific direction and send data to several users at the same transmission time interval (TTI) via the same carrier or resource block (RB). Antenna arrays usually contain up to 64 single antennas. We have been modeled the process of the data transmission from the cell to the user device or user equipment (UE), have been formulated mathematical abstraction of the resource allocation problem, and have been proposed a lightweight algorithm that uses a proportional fair metric.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Channel Frequency-Correlation in an Indoor Multipath Environment for Wireless Key Generation
abstract: Channel randomness in wireless communication systems can be employed for generating two copies of a key bits sequence in a given pair of nodes. Among others, the differential phase method that uses phase samples of two coherent frequency tones for generating high-entropy key bits sequence seems to be a promising technique. Unfortunately, implementation of the differential phase method relies on correct specification of the frequency separation of the probing tones, which requires additional study of the frequency-correlation properties of the propagation medium. This paper is devoted to experimental study of the channel frequency-correlation properties in a typical indoor environment. Frequency autocorrelation functions are experimentally determined for the signal envelope and carrier phase on four different indoor radio links. The estimates of the channel coherence bandwidth and multipath delay spread are performed, and the influence of the line-of-sight component (LOS) is considered. Our experiments showed that, depending on the LOS intensity, the coherence bandwidth on typical indoor radio links of 20-meters length varies from 8 MHz to 25 MHz (for the correlation level of 0.2), whereas for samples of the carrier phase, the coherence bandwidth is somewhat narrower and varies from 6 MHz to 19 MHz.
